ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All directors, shareholders, ultimate beneficial owners, counterparties, target vessels, bunker suppliers, delivery agents, and payment remitters must undergo mandatory screening against the Korean Financial Intelligence Unit designated list, Overseas Assets-Control Sanctions list, United Nations Security Council consolidated financial sanctions list, United States OFAC SDN list, and European Union financial sanctions list. Enhanced due diligence must include identification of politically exposed persons, verification of source of funds, beneficial ownership concentration at the 25 percent threshold, negative news and adverse media checks, independent corporate chain piercing, ongoing transaction monitoring, risk-based escalation, and immediate retention of suspicious transaction reports when any sanctions match or red flag appears. The screening protocol must be updated whenever a new sanctions designation is published and must be fully documented before incorporation, bank account opening, vessel chartering, or issuance of any standby letter of credit.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Electronic Registration Office (iRO / Internet Registration Office) and nationwide Korean Company Registry system
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A Chusik Hoesa must be registered using a Hangul statutory name. Non-Korean legal names and brand names must be transliterated phonetically into Hangul and must include the mandatory legal-form suffix 'Chusik Hoesa' (주식회사). The four-tier naming convention is: (1) distinctive main trade name, (2) descriptive business purpose corresponding to the Korean Standard Industrial Classification for marine fuel supply, (3) location of the principal office, and (4) legal-form suffix. Latin characters, Arabic numerals, and symbols may be used only as auxiliary or trading style elements and cannot replace the Hangul registration name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Korean registration office rejects a proposed Chusik Hoesa name, the filer must submit a written objection within seven days of the rejection together with a corrected name clearance application and a memorandum explaining why the name is distinctive and does not infringe an existing trade name. If the registry maintains the rejection, legal counsel may file an administrative appeal with the competent administrative court under the Administrative Litigation Act within 90 days of the rejection notice. Alternatively, the filer may resubmit an alternative name after obtaining a fresh availability and conflict search report from the iRO and Korean trademark databases. The entire rejection and appeal process should be documented for the due diligence record.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mail-forwarding address is not permissible as the sole registered address for a Chusik Hoesa engaged in offshore marine fuel bunkering and lubricant replenishment. The Korean National Tax Service requires an actual business premises where tax records, business registration certificate, board minutes, and bunker supply contracts are physically accessible, and where official service of process can be delivered. The coastal municipal authority issuing the petroleum sales or marine bunkering license will require a physical office with a registered address that appears on the business registration certificate. A serviced office that provides a real work desk, permanent local management, and meeting rooms may satisfy commercial substance requirements, but a private virtual mailbox or post-office forwarding address will be rejected by the tax office, registry, and bunkering licensing authority.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist for unannounced physical inspections: (1) business registration certificate displayed at the registered office; (2) original tax invoices and bunker delivery records maintained on site; (3) employment records of at least one resident employee or director; (4) bank statements reconciling fuel purchases and sales; (5) vessel and bunker barge licensing documents; (6) written contractual evidence of fuel storage or terminal arrangements; (7) compliance manual with AML/CFT procedures. Quantified risk: at least 60 percent likelihood of an unannounced inspection within the first 12 months after business registration and bunkering license issuance, followed by a recurring audit cycle of two to four inspections per year for marine fuel suppliers.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea; online electronic portal: HomeTax (https://www.hometax.go.kr); export and customs declarations coordinated through Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS (https://unipass.customs.go.kr)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign non-resident entity engaged in marine bunkering in Korea, the statutory procedure is: (1) identify whether the foreign entity has a Korean permanent establishment or fixed place of business; if yes, apply for the ten-digit Business Registration Number (BRN) with the district tax office of the National Tax Service using the 'Application for Business Registration' on HomeTax within 20 days of commencing business; (2) if there is no domestic place of business but taxable supplies occur in Korea or a VAT refund/zero-rating claim is intended, file the business registration as a foreign non-resident business operator and, if required, appoint a tax representative with a domestic address under the National Tax Basic Act; the BRN is also the VAT identification number and no separate VAT ID is issued; (3) submit corporate constitutive documents (certificate of existence, articles of incorporation), a board resolution confirming the Korean business operator, power of attorney for the tax representative, identification of the registered executive, proof of the Korean bank account or bonded fuel storage/agency arrangement, and the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries marine fuel supply license where the bunkering business is legally carried on; (4) upon approval, NTS issues a business registration certificate and the BRN must be used for all e-tax invoices, customs declarations, and VAT returns.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None available of the check-the-box type; Korean tax classification is determined by law and a Chusik Hoesa cannot elect pass-through treatment. Hybrid mismatch rules under the Adjustment of International Tax Act apply to cross-border entities and instruments; domestic consolidated corporate tax filing is available only for qualified wholly owned Korean subsidiaries and is not an entity classification election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Korean Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act, administered by the National Tax Service
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No KRW turnover threshold; under Article 5 of the Value-Added Tax Act a new business must file for business registration within 20 days from commencement. A Chusik Hoesa must register even if its marine bunkering turnover is entirely zero-rated export, and there is no simplified-taxpayer threshold for a corporation.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic tax invoices apply under Article 32 of the Value-Added Tax Act for every business-to-business taxable supply, including zero-rated marine bunkering. Each Chusik Hoesa must issue the e-tax invoice through the HomeTax e-invoice system and transmit the invoice data to NTS on the day of issue or no later than one day thereafter, using the official HomeTax API, FAS, or an accredited e-invoice ASP. Paper tax invoices are not permitted for corporate suppliers except in narrowly defined statutory exceptions. The NTS records an electronic issue number and digital signature-equivalent control, and cross-matches e-tax invoices with Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS export declarations and foreign exchange settlement records. For onshore retail sales, a HomeTax electronic cash receipt is required for B2C transactions; bunkering B2B supplies are covered by e-tax invoices.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Article 26 of the Value-Added Tax Act and related NTS marine bunkering guidance, zero percent VAT applies to goods exported from Korea and to supplies qualifying as international maritime transport support. Marine fuel, bunkers and lubricants supplied to ocean-going vessels engaged in international voyages in Korean ports qualify for zero-rating when the vessel is in international service, the fuel is physically delivered on board at a Korean port, the vessel proceeds to a foreign destination, and the sale is supported by export declaration or bunkering-equivalent customs or port records and is settled in foreign exchange under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. Qualifying offshore digital services are not part of this marine bunkering scope.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Korea Customs Service export declaration (UNI-PASS electronic declaration number), together with the bunker delivery note / delivery receipt and the bonded fuel stock record for the bunkering operation

Original or certified copy of the Bill of Lading (or, for bunkering, the vessel international voyage call record with IMO number, port rotation and departure certificate from a Korean port to a foreign destination)

Foreign exchange proceeds settlement confirmation from a Korean foreign exchange bank (foreign exchange transaction record / inward remittance record) evidencing receipt of the marine fuel export proceeds within the statutory repatriation period
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: NTS and Korea Customs Service routinely reconcile e-tax invoices, UNI-PASS export declarations, bunker delivery records and bank foreign-exchange settlement confirmations. If documentation is missing, inaccurate, or export proceeds are not received within the 180-day repatriation window, the zero-rating is disallowed, the supply is re-characterized as domestic taxable, and NTS will assess 10% VAT plus interest and the statutory penalty surcharges for false returns, including the highest-tier 40% penalty for fraudulent or fabricated export evidence and underpayment penalties for negligent misreporting. Additional consequences include suspension or revocation of the marine fuel supply license by the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries, criminal liability under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, and penalties under the Customs Duty Act for false export declarations, with assessment limitation periods extended in cases of fraud or cross-border transactions.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The Bank of Korea (BOK) as central bank, with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) as the foreign exchange policy and regulatory authority under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act; enforcement is delegated to the Korea Customs Service for documentary reporting and to the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit for AML surveillance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea maintains a broadly open current-account regime for trade settlements, but capital and financial account operations remain subject to filing, licensing, or notification requirements. The Korean won is fully convertible for most genuine business transactions within the declared banking system, but all cross-border payments must flow through recognized foreign exchange banks and be reported to the Foreign Exchange Information System (FEIS). Export proceeds from marine bunkering sales must be receipted within the statutory trade settlement window (normally 90 days from shipment) and may be held in a domestic nominated foreign-currency account or converted to KRW at the onshore commercial bank exchange rate; mandatory surrender was effectively abolished in Korea, so the treasury may retain USD or other settlement currencies for future fueling purchases. Profit remittances to non-resident shareholders are lawful but subjected to a strict documentary trail: audited financial statements, corporate tax clearance, undistributed earnings verification, and the underlying foreign exchange bank's trade settlement report. Because KRW is not fully deliverable offshore, the Chusik Hoesa must keep its payment, hedging, and settlement relationships inside the Korean banking system and should avoid unlicensed digital EMIs that lack the statutory foreign exchange bank designation needed for valid capital and trade settlement reporting.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds must be received within 90 days from the date of shipment under the BOK trade settlement rules; an extension of up to one additional 90-day period or longer is available only with documented justification and, where required, prior approval from the MOEF/BOK. There is no mandatory minimum conversion ratio currently in force, so proceeds may be retained in foreign currency in a domestic foreign-currency account or converted to KRW at a licensed foreign exchange bank; every receipt must be reported with its export declaration number in FEIS and supported by a matching customs export confirmation.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore digital EMI platforms are not legally viable as primary treasury rails for a Korean-resident Chusik Hoesa. In South Korea, only licensed foreign exchange banks and locally authorized financial services providers may operate cross-border payment, foreign exchange settlement, and KRW clearing services; offshore EMIs cannot hold KRW directly, cannot provide a Korean bank account, and are not permitted to file the FDI or trade settlement reports required under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. Any EMI that relies on a partner bank license in another European or UAE jurisdiction will be deemed unlicensed for Korean capital/trade settlement purposes, raising automatic AML rejections. A fintech partner may be used only as a secondary reporting/cash-flow visualization layer if the actual MT103 settlement continues through a domestic tier-1 bank, and even then it adds compliance burden without reducing the in-branch KYC mandate.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In practice, the representative director and the signatories must appear in person at a Korean tier-1 bank branch to complete the Real Name Financial Transactions Act identity verification and the mandatory corporate KYC interview, unless the bank accepts a consular-notarized and apostilled power of attorney under strict internal risk-appetite policies. Most Korean banks require at least one natural-person Korean-resident signatory for daily operation of the KRW account, while non-resident directors may verify their identity via a Korean consulate abroad and authorize an in-country company officer or statutory agent to attend the interview. Remote video-only onboarding is not accepted for a foreign-owned Chusik Hoesa; the bank will demand the certified articles of incorporation, shareholder registry, UBO certificates, passport copies with notarized translation, company sealing register, board resolutions, and physical proof of the Korean registered office.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Newly incorporated Chusik Hoesa whose entire ownership is non-resident and whose registered address is a law-firm or tax-agent office.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the certificate of incorporation, audited or pro-forma financial statements, stockholders ledger, UBO declaration with passport copies and REAL NAME verification, Korean tax registration and office lease copy, board resolution authorizing the bank mandate, and proof of foreign direct investment report filed with the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy or KOTRA.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: No beneficial owner or managing director has a verifiable face-to-face presence in South Korea, and the company presents no local operating history in marine bunkering.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver apostilled and consular-certified powers of attorney for an in-country representative, notarized passport copies of all UBOs, a forward-dated business plan with physical barge/pier supplier contracts, a Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries ship-bunkering license or application acknowledgment, P&I insurance certificates, and IMO registration details of the supply vessels.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Heavy cross-border payment profile with short settlement times and repeated international bunker invoices, raising sanctions and trade-based money laundering risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a counterparty wallet/vessel blocklist, sanctions-cleared customer list, certified bunker supply agreements containing charter party references, port authority gate/boarding records, operational invoices and bills of lading, bank trade reporting history, vessel IMO numbers, crew and beneficial-ownership screening reports, and a corporate AML manual approved by the bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of inbound equity capital appears to come from a high-risk offshore holding company or through an unfettered digital payment corridor.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Supply the full chain of source-of-funds documentation: audited parent company accounts, tax clearance/certificate of good standing from the UBO jurisdiction, 12 months of bank statements for the remitting account, SWIFT MT103 payment history, signed declarations confirming no nominee or unlicensed intermediary has been used, and a group organizational chart evidencing the economic purpose of the Korean bunkering subsidiary.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Equity capital must be remitted through a SWIFT MT103 to the Chusik Hoesa's Capital Escrow Account maintained at a Korean foreign exchange bank, and the remitter must cite the foreign exchange purpose code for Direct Investment Capital Contribution under the Foreign Exchange Information System (FEIS). The inward transfer must be matched to the prior FDI notification or post-export report filed with the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy or KOTRA; the bank will issue a foreign-currency deposit certificate / capital verification confirmation which must be used to register the foreign investment and until that registration is accepted the account cannot be treated as equity. For operating cash flows, all bunkering receivables must be received through the same licensed FX bank and tagged with the export trade settlement code; trade intercompany loans and operational injections require documented loan contracts or service agreements and must avoid offshore EMIs or third-country clearing entities to prevent FEIS mismatches and KRW non-deliverable issues.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade payments for bunker fuel, lubricants, port fees, barge maintenance and crew-related costs will be executed through the local foreign exchange bank using SWIFT MT103 wire transfers with precise invoice maturity codes; the bank requires the source trade contracts, invoice, shipping documents and final settlement instructions. For high-value or recurring fuel purchases, a commercial documentary letter of credit is preferable because it preserves title and provides the bank with an independent examination of port delivery evidence. Standby LCs are appropriate as bid bonds or performance guarantees for terminal/port operators and major shipping clients, while documentary collections are permitted for direct bunker suppliers but expose the treasury to goods-covered-by-document timing risk. The treasury must ensure that each disbursement is aligned to an underlying real transaction and that FEIS outbound reporting codes match the stated economic substance, as Korean banks are required to reject unbacked cross-border transfers.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore forward foreign-exchange contracts executed with the Korean foreign exchange bank solely to hedge USD/KRW and EUR/KRW exposures arising from identified bunkering invoices or receivable contracts with maturity within the underlying trade cycle

Short-term currency swaps, up to one-year tenor, used to align USD funding needed for bunker fuel procurement with the KRW revenue stream, provided the nominal amount is linked to actual trade cash flows
Bank-approved rolling hedging is allowed only with a negative mark-to-market margin mechanism; speculative uncovered foreign-exchange options are not permitted

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are restricted because KRW is not freely deliverable offshore and are not usable for an onshore Chusik Hoesa without MOEF/BOK approval or unless the underlying exposure is itself non-deliverable and so justified; speculative NDF positions are prohibited
Natural hedge pass-through clauses with bunker suppliers under which the invoice currency and price-adjustment formula is agreed to reduce residual FX exposure

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return and Local Income Tax Surcharge Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service through HomeTax and the competent local government through the WeTax local tax system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the end of the fiscal year; for a calendar-year Chusik Hoesa, no later than March 31 of the immediately following tax year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or omitted filing triggers an underreporting addition of 20% of the unpaid corporate tax (40% if the omission is fraudulent), plus daily overdue interest of 0.022% on the unpaid tax and local income tax surcharge; continued delinquency triggers forced collection and seizure of property under the National Tax Collection Act, cancellation of the business registration certificate, and court-ordered dissolution if the company loses its place of business and its directors cannot be located.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Settlement Financial Statements and Annual General Meeting Approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Meeting of Shareholders; minutes and approved financial statements must be kept at the company's registered head office and made available for inspection under the Korean Commercial Act
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The Annual General Meeting and approval of the settlement financial statements must be completed within three months after the end of the fiscal year; for a calendar-year company, by March 31
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to prepare the required financial statements or to convene the Annual General Meeting exposes directors to administrative fines of KRW 10,000,000; an irregular settlement may invalidate dividends, trigger corrective tax reassessments, and constitute a ground for an adverse audit opinion.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Audited Financial Statements and External Auditor's Report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service through the Data Analysis, Retrieval and Transfer (DART) electronic disclosure system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within four months after the end of the fiscal year; for a calendar-year company subject to mandatory external audit, by April 30
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to submit the statutory auditor's report to the FSS by the statutory deadline attracts fines of up to KRW 30,000,000 under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies; the company may be placed on the FSS non-disclosure list, and tax authorities may reject the unaudited financial statements when assessing corporate income tax.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership and Shareholding Register Maintenance Confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company's principal office; no separate annual public filing for ordinary private stock companies unless the company is a listed or financial institution subject to FSS and FIU reporting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The Register of Members must be current as of the Annual General Meeting date; any share transfer, pledge, or change of beneficial ownership must be recorded within 30 days of the triggering event
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to update the Register of Members does not invalidate the transfer between the parties but prevents the transferee from exercising corporate rights against the company; repeated inaccuracy creates director civil liability, shareholder inspection claims, and adverse AML/CDD consequences with Korean financial institutions.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory statutory independent CPA audit applies to: (a) every corporation listed on the Korea Exchange (KOSPI/KOSDAQ); (b) financial institutions, insurance companies, and other public-interest companies subject to external audit under separate statutes; and (c) any unlisted Chusik Hoesa whose total assets at the end of the immediately preceding business year equal or exceed KRW 12 billion (approximately USD 9.2 million). No general turnover or headcount threshold is prescribed for ordinary private marine bunkering companies; however, an audit may be required contractually by lenders, by a K-IFRS consolidating parent, or by supervisory designation of the Financial Services Commission.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: K-IFRS (Korean International Financial Reporting Standards) is mandatory for listed and public-interest companies; non-listed Chusik Hoesa entities subject to external audit may apply K-GAAP, and eligible small or medium enterprises may apply the Accounting Standards for Small and Medium-Sized Companies (ASSSME). All financial statements must comply with the accrual-basis recordkeeping requirements of the Corporate Tax Act, and the chosen framework must be applied consistently.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Korea does not impose a standalone annual universal beneficial ownership return for ordinary private stock corporations. However, under the Korean Commercial Act, the Register of Members must be kept accurate at the head office, and a transfer of registered shares must be entered in that register before the transferee can exercise shareholder rights against the company. Under Korean AML and real-name financial transaction rules, financial institutions providing banking or payment rails must identify beneficial owners at onboarding and refresh that information on an ongoing basis; the company is expected to report any change in beneficial ownership or shareholding structure to its bank within 30 days to avoid account restrictions. Listed and financial-company cases are subject to additional FSS and Korea FIU periodic filings.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 6,000 - USD 20,000 per certified audit engagement for a mid-sized non-listed bunkering company; larger or consolidated groups will exceed this range

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 21% national corporate income tax top marginal rate; 23.1% combined effective rate when the 10% local income tax surcharge is included
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Quasi-dormant for bunkering: 5-year 100% corporate income tax exemption plus 2-year 50% reduction for qualifying foreign-invested high-tech enterprises in Free Economic Zones (Foreign Investment Promotion Act); R&D expenditure credits up to 30-40% under the Restriction of Special Taxation Act; venture/SME reduced rates on the first KRW 200 million of taxable income; no dedicated tax holiday for ship bunkering or lubricant replenishment

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Base and Final Return (Article 60 of the Corporate Tax Act, prescribed return form together with local income tax schedule); mandatory electronic filing through the national HomeTax portal (hometax.go.kr)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; interim tax prepayments are due in August during the fiscal year
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Fiscal year ending 31 December: domestic Chusik Hoesa must file by 31 March of the following year; foreign corporation with a domestic place of business must file by 30 April of the following year; next business day applies if the statutory date falls on a holiday.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate identification, tax registration number, head office address, representative director's name and TIN, and HomeTax user credentials.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Schedule the foreign shareholder's country, TIN, and ownership percentage. If the director or tax representative is a non-resident, register a Korean tax agent. Omission will cause automatic issuance of a 22% non-resident withholding certificate for all later outbound payments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal year dates, accounting basis (accrual), K-IFRS or K-GAAP adoption, and type of business under Korean Standard Industry Classification (ISIC 5222 marine bunkering).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Even if the foreign parent uses a non-calendar fiscal year, the Korean entity file is separate. Accrual accounting is mandatory; cash-basis treatment is prohibited for this entity class.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Sales and revenue lines: bunker fuel sales, lubricant sales, slop disposal services, logistics and incidental income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report gross bunker revenue at arm's length FOB or delivered-ex-ship value. When title passes in Korean waters or contract negotiation occurs through the Korean office, the income is Korean-source. Retain delivery receipts, port logs and vessel lists to prove cross-border supply.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of goods sold and operating expenses: fuel product purchases, tanker charter, port charges, storage costs, crew, insurance, depreciation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign-currency purchases must be converted using the transaction-date exchange rate. Any intercompany fuel purchase must be benchmarked under the arm's length standard; service fees paid to non-residents for ship brokerage or blending know-how are subject to 22% withholding unless a tax treaty claim is filed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductions and tax adjustments: entertainment disallowances, bad debt additions, prior-period corrections, non-deductible taxes and penalties.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Intercompany management charges and royalties require economic substance and contemporaneous documentation; if recharacterized as a disguised dividend, the distribution element will attract additional withholding tax on repatriation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income before loss carryforward and net operating loss application.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Korean entity may apply NOL carryforward for up to 10 years; large corporations are limited to 60% of current taxable income and SMEs to 100%. Non-resident parent losses cannot be netted against the Korean entity's income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of tax: KRW 0-200 million at 9%; KRW 200 million - 20 billion at 19%; above KRW 20 billion at 21%; local income tax surcharge of 10% of the national tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute local income tax simultaneously. When treaty reduced rates have been granted for dividend distributions, separate the schedule of distributable profits and confirm no double exemption from both treaty and domestic law.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign tax credit, interim prepayments, R&D credits, employment credits, and prepaid withholding tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the Korean entity is also taxed in another port state on international bunkering sales, attach a foreign tax credit return together with foreign assessment documents. Do not claim credits on taxes paid by the foreign parent or the non-resident beneficial owner.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Attached supplementary schedules: financial statements, audit report if applicable, transaction with related parties, controlled foreign company schedules, and tax treaty filings.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a foreign-controlled Chusik Hoesa, attach full intercompany transaction schedules. If payments to non-residents have been made, attach the withholding tax declaration and show the treaty articles used for reduced rates.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or non-filing of the corporate income tax return triggers a negligence penalty of 20% of the tax unpaid for failure to file; 10% for under-reporting; and 40% for fraudulent under-reporting. Interest accrues daily at 0.022%. Failure to attach transfer pricing documentation or required supplementary schedules incurs separate administrative fines. Criminal tax evasion under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act is punishable by imprisonment up to 5 years and can extend to 10 years in aggravated cases, with fines up to five times the evaded amount.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% statutory withholding on non-resident dividends (20% national tax plus 2% local income tax surcharge); treaty rates typically reduce this to 10-15% or higher under applicable DTA depending on shareholding.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before paying a dividend, interest, or royalty to a non-resident, the Korean payer must file a treaty claim through HomeTax with: (i) a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the foreign jurisdiction for the calendar year of payment; (ii) a Form for Non-Taxation/Exemption Under Tax Treaty, including a beneficial ownership declaration; (iii) board resolutions and ownership structure evidencing that the recipient is not a conduit, nominee, or agent; (iv) evidence of economic substance of the recipient (premises, employees, business activity), especially for dividends on substantial shareholdings. The payments can be made at the treaty rate only after NTS review or an effective domestic law self-assessment. If full 22% is withheld, the non-resident may apply for refund within the five-year statute of limitations.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding on cross-border interest and royalties is also 22% (20% national plus 2% local). Under Korea's bilateral treaties, royalty rates are frequently capped at 10-15% and interest at 10-15%; for example, the Korea-US DTA commonly reduces dividends to 15% (10% for qualified 10% shareholders), interest to 10%, and royalties to 15%. Payments for vessel bunkering software, trademarked fuel additives, or lubricant formulas must be analyzed for the industrial royalty definition under the treaty and may be recharacterized if the payer has no real use of the intangible in Korea.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Statutory transfer pricing documentation (Local File) is required in Korea when the value of related-party transactions in a business year exceeds KRW 10 billion by transaction type. A Master File is additionally required when the multinational group's consolidated revenue is at least KRW 1 trillion and the Korean entity's aggregate related-party transactions exceed KRW 50 billion.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea has not enacted a UAE-style economic substance regulation but applies the substance-over-form doctrine through Article 14 of the Framework Act on National Taxes and Supreme Court precedent on sham transactions. Korean CFC rules may re-attribute passive income of an offshore affiliate. For ship bunkering, the Chusik Hoesa must demonstrate local capacity by owning or leasing storage tanks, retaining traders and operations staff, maintaining marine fuel supply licenses from the relevant Korean authorities, and making strategic decisions in Korea; otherwise the NTS can disregard the Korean entity as a conduit and deny treaty benefits under the OECD Multilateral Instrument Principal Purpose Test.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion – Concealment of Bunker Sales Revenue
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Chusik Hoesa maintains two ledger sets: a physical delivery ledger for international vessels and a declared ledger for the NTS. Unrecorded bunkering proceeds are routed through the non-resident parent's offshore bank accounts. False invoices are prepared for fuel losses and port charges to reduce the declared taxable base.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, Article 3, deliberate tax evasion carries imprisonment of up to 5 years, extendable to 10 years for aggravated amounts, plus a fine up to five times the evaded tax. The NTS may also impose a 40% fraudulent return negligence penalty and 0.022% daily late interest; the local petroleum business license can be suspended or revoked.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false returns face secondary tax liability under Article 39 of the National Tax Collection Act, allowing the NTS to seize personal assets for unpaid corporate taxes. A departure ban (travel blacklisting) may be issued until taxes and penalties are settled. In aggravated evasion cases, the de facto foreign controller and the resident director may be jointly prosecuted and sentenced to imprisonment with extradition/travel-bloc consequences.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Fraud – Sham Intercompany Fees and Missing Documentation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The foreign parent sells bunker fuel to the Korean entity at inflated prices while the Korean entity receives no mark-up for its supply chain management; the same profits are shifted as a 15% 'royalty' for a trademark owned by a zero-tax affiliate staffed by zero employees. The Korean entity exceeds the KRW 10 billion Local File threshold but fails to prepare contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation and does not file a Master File despite group revenue above KRW 1 trillion.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Corporate Tax Act Article 52, the NTS may disregard the intercompany prices and recompute taxable income on the basis of an arm's length comparable, giving rise to additional tax at 21%, an underreporting penalty of 10-20%, and daily interest. Missing transfer pricing documentation results in separate fines of up to KRW 100 million and is treated as an index of willful neglect.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who authorized the sham intercompany fees can be held personally liable for the resulting tax arrears under the National Tax Collection Act. If the transfer pricing arrangement is used to strip assets from Korea, the civil alter-ego doctrine supports piercing the corporate veil, and the directors may be charged criminally for evasion, receiving travel bans, asset garnishment, and imprisonment terms of up to 5 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company, Money Laundering, and Treaty Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Korean Chusik Hoesa exists only as a mailbox: no office, no full-time staff, no marine fuel storage, no valid bunkering license, and a bank account that channels SWIFT payments from high-risk flag vessels to the foreign beneficiary. Beneficial ownership declarations are false, and no suspicious transaction reports are filed despite irregular commission flows.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Act on Reporting and Use of Specific Financial Transaction Information imposes criminal fines and imprisonment for AML violations; the lacking petroleum license can be revoked under the Petroleum Business Act; the court may order dissolution of the company for abuse of corporate form under the Commercial Act. The tax authority will deny treaty advantages under the MLI's Principal Purpose Test, causing 22% withholding on all non-resident remittances and full corporate income tax on the deemed Korean PE.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Nominee directors are jointly and severally liable for damages to creditors under Commercial Act Article 401; they face criminal prosecution for false beneficial ownership declarations and AML reporting failures, with imprisonment up to 5 years and fines up to KRW 50 million. The NTS will also lift the corporate veil in civil collection, freeze assets, impose departure restrictions, and seek personal recovery of the full corporate liability from the foreign beneficial owner acting as de facto director.
